sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:42

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:42:1
items.html:
It returned to be Mati in Keter; it was Lo Mati in Hochma and Bina, etc.: You already know that the arrival of Hesed in its own vessel causes it to be Mati in Keter, as above, page 328, the passage beginning “and you find.” For there is no giving of lights except face to face, as the ARI says above; and if so, Bina must refine from phase two to phase one, and then the lights of HB depart to Keter and cause an upper coupling there, on the coarseness of phase three, and once more the light is Mati in Keter at the level of Hochma, as at first. And then it is Lo Mati in HB, for the posterior of the vessel of Keter stops and detains the illumination of GAR, as above. And because of this it is Lo Mati in Hesed as well, for there are two distances that are empty, without light, which are HB; and since the light is not Mati in Hochma, that illumination of Hochma which is in Hesed is likewise cut off from it, and Hesed returned to its Katnut, and once more it needs its mother Bina, to nurse the illumination of GAR from her, as above. And therefore Hesed rises to Bina, and its vessel turns its face downward, and once more the light of Gvura descends to the vessel of Gvura, and it is found to be Mati in Gvura. And then it is Lo Mati in Tifferet, for the posterior of Gvura stops and detains the illumination of GAR of the light of Tifferet; and therefore the light of Tifferet rises to the vessel of Gvura, for it descended from Gvura only by the force of the illumination of GAR of the rule of Hesed over Gvura, as above, and now that the rule of Gvura has returned, Gvura raises its light to her as at first.
And then the vessel of Tifferet turns its face downward, for it must annul its bestowal of GAR, which had been its face before this, and make its posterior into the face of bestowal; and then it lowers the remainder of the light in it to Netzah. And this is called Mati in Netzah.
Now we shall thoroughly understand the Sefira of Netzah of ZA. For the vessel of Netzah is the aspect of ZA itself, since the fourth Hesed of the five Hassadim stands opposite phase three of Keter and the four phases of direct light, as above; for the HGT are the aspects of KHB of the Hassadim, and Netzah and Hod are the aspects of ZA and Malchut of the Hassadim. And you find that from the side of the light, the Sefira of Tifferet is the essence of the light of ZA, as above, for the very substance of the light of Da'at clothes in the vessel of Tifferet; and this is by reason of the exchange of the lights, for since the light of Hochma clothed in Keter and the light of Bina in the vessel of Hochma, the light of ZA is found to have clothed in the vessel of Bina. And therefore, among the five Hassadim, the light of ZA is found to clothe in the vessel of Tifferet, which is the aspect of Bina of the five Hassadim, as above. However, from the side of the vessels, Netzah is considered the substance of ZA, as above. And the light of Netzah is the aspect of the VAK that remained in the vessel of Tifferet after its departure from there to Gvura, as above. And the difference between it and the Sefira of Gvura is this: that the light of Gvura, although it too is the aspect of VAK, is nevertheless of the value of the VAK of Hochma, for it is the remainder of Hesed from the aspect of the illumination of Hochma in it, and it is of the value of the light of the ZON of the vessel of Bina; whereas the light of Netzah is the aspect of the VAK of the light of ZA, for it was explained that the light of Tifferet is the aspect of the light of ZA in its very substance.
And chiefly one must discern here that the relation of the lights and the vessels of HGT to the lights and the vessels of NHYM is like the relation of GAR to VAK, since the HGT stand opposite the GAR of the five phases, and NHYM stand opposite ZA and Malchut of the five phases, as explained.
